title: Batch scoring, monitoring, and the drift that arrives without an announcement

videos.script: January the first, 2026. The model scores four thousand subscribers and keeps the file. {{run}} On the day, only the inputs can be checked. A plan the model has never seen, and a price alarm that has been ringing since September. {{inputs}} A month later the answers arrive. The ranking held. The level did not, and the credits earned less than half of what the chances promised. {{labels}} Broken down by group, two cities stand out, and nothing in the inputs had moved. A competitor opened there in January. {{cities}} Refitting fixes the new plan and the overall level, and not the competitor. {{refit}} By the end, the frame from lesson one has its last rows: what is checked every month, and who is told. {{end}}
